name: Re-read text
howTo: Find some writing, read it, look away, then read it again and see whether it stayed the same.
evidence: LaBerge calls this the best test and advises using the same test each time. The Lucidity Institute states text changes 75% of the time when re-read once and 95% when re-read twice in dreams; that is the Institute's own figure, not an independent trial. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Digital clock
howTo: Look at a digital watch or clock, look away, then look again and check that it shows a sensible time both times.
evidence: LaBerge: in a dream it "will never behave correctly". Analog watches can show plausible dream time, so they are not reliable, and low-battery style explanations are a trap. No independent study of this test alone was found. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Memory test
howTo: Think back over the last several minutes and notice whether you have any trouble remembering what just happened and how you got here.
evidence: Tholey calls recalling the preceding period one of the most effective tests, and LaBerge includes it, but this is expert judgement rather than a controlled result. Tholey warns it fails against false awakenings, so pair it with the light switch on waking. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Light switch
howTo: On any apparent awakening, turn a light on; if it does not come on, suspect you are still dreaming.
evidence: Recommended by Tholey specifically for false awakenings, where the memory test fails. A failing switch fits LaBerge's object action signs (malfunctioning devices). Recommended by Tholey, not tested in a trial. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Tholey's 180-degree turn
howTo: Turn 180 degrees and try to stand still; in a dream the body may keep turning or the surroundings may revolve.
evidence: A physical test from Tholey's own overview of his method. Described by its author, not tested in a trial. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Nose pinch
howTo: Close your lips, pinch your nose shut and try to breathe in; if air still flows, you are dreaming.
evidence: Community practice, not from LaBerge. Used as one of the two tests in Aspy's studies. No primary study of its own reliability was located. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Finger through palm
howTo: Push a finger against your other palm and try to pass it through; if it goes through, you are dreaming.
evidence: Community practice, not from LaBerge. Used as one of the two tests in Aspy's studies. No primary study of its own reliability was located. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Counting fingers
howTo: Look at your hand and count your fingers slowly, then count them once more and see whether the number holds.
evidence: Widely used community check with no known originator and no primary study of its reliability; offer it as an option, make no claim of evidence. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Jumping
howTo: Hop and try to stay in the air; staying up even a split second longer than normal means you are dreaming.
evidence: LaBerge gives a try-to-fly version of this test; jumping itself is a widely used community check with no known originator. No primary study of its reliability was located. Caveat: reality testing on its own showed no benefit for lucid dreaming in the induction studies (RESEARCH.md Part B, sections 3.3 and 3.12: Aspy 2017 and 2020, B37 and B38), so do not expect any single check to bring on lucidity.

name: Mirror
howTo: Look at your face in a mirror and check whether it looks the way it should and stays the same.
evidence: Widespread community check with no primary study of its reliability located; offer it as an option, make no claim of evidence. Seeing yourself in a mirror is also a typical dream theme reported by 15.9% of students.
